items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: this kid put the lyrics to it, this Copeland. He says, one of the writers.

ctx.x: No, just put all the names down.

So, years later, after 28 years, you suppose a copywriter tune, I didn't figure, I figured it was nothing. Because I was getting $12 and $8 on, you know, the royalties. So one day I hear this thing, take me in your arms and never let me go. I says, man, that's Tin Roof, note for note. So I call up Teenie, that's Captain Harris' sister, that's Paul's wife. So I says, Teenie, have you got the copyright on Tin Roof? She says, yes, and you can thank me because I just had it renewed because those guys had it,…
Yeah. Is there anything of interest to your trombone soul, how you first, you might say, created that thing, you know, starting on that low note and all?
